paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God is the One who decides who rules, and He told His people to trust that, even when it hurt. He says, "By My great power and outstretched arm, I made the earth and the men and beasts on the face of it, and I give it to whom I please." (Jeremiah 27:5) So when the LORD tells Judah to put their necks under Babylon's yoke, He is asking them to serve that king by trusting the One who made the earth.

Now here's the hard part: the other voices were saying what everybody wanted to hear, and God calls it "a lie." (Jeremiah 27:10) I think a comfortable word is the hardest kind to turn down, because it feels so good going in. Jeremiah's message was "serve him and his people, and live!" (Jeremiah 27:12), not the easy word but the one that led to life. And God said He had not sent those other prophets (Jeremiah 27:15).

So, baker, when a voice tells you what you hope is true, test it against what God has actually said. Don't ask whether it feels good; ask whether it's His word. And hold on to this too: even for the articles carried off to Babylon, God says He will "bring them back and restore them to this place." (Jeremiah 27:22) His timing is not ours, and I should know, because I waited years in a drawer, but this story isn't over, friend, and there's more teaching still to come.
